The Eolos Wind Energy Research Station at the University of Minnesota consists of a 2.5 MW wind turbine and a 130 m meteorological tower.
The selected one-hour dataset had a mean wind direction of 178° at hub height with a small deviation of 3.7°, and a mean wind speed of 7.8 m/s.
The turbulence intensity ranged from 13% at the bottom tip to 5% at the top tip of the rotor during the selected period.
The boundary layer frequency (f_L) was about 0.01 Hz, and the rotor frequency (f_D) was about 0.08 Hz.
The normalized flapwise blade root bending moment varied from -1.0 to 1.0, indicating moments along and against the rotation direction.

The flapwise bending moment spectrum exhibited a dominant peak at the turbine rotational frequency (f = 0.22 Hz), in contrast to the foundation strain spectrum which peaked at the blade passing frequency (f_BPF = 0.66 Hz).
The edgewise bending moment spectrum showed strong peaks at 0.97 Hz and 3.1 Hz, associated with the undamped natural frequency of the collective blade pitch control.
The magnitude of the high-pressure strain power spectrum increased outward from the blade root due to increased blade elasticity.
The high-pressure and low-pressure side strain spectra matched well with a slope of f^-5/3 to f^-2 in the lower and intermediate frequency ranges.
The leading-edge and trailing-edge regions of the blade were much less responsive to the turbulent inflow in the lower and intermediate frequency ranges.

The normalized fluctuation (standard deviation) of the flapwise bending moment was higher than that of the edgewise bending moment, suggesting higher sensitivity to the change of turbine structural configuration.
The researchers applied several restrictions on wind direction, yaw error, turbine operating conditions, and atmospheric stability to select the one-hour dataset for analysis.
The blade sensor system used fiber-optic strain gauges installed at different radial positions along each blade to measure the blade deformation.
The researchers leveraged the unique facility of the Eolos Wind Energy Research Station, which has a well-instrumented 2.5 MW wind turbine and a meteorological tower, to conduct this field study.

The researchers calculated the edgewise and flapwise blade root bending moments from the strain gauge measurements at the leading-edge, trailing-edge, high-pressure, and low-pressure regions of the blade cross-section.
